```{=html}

Join the EC² Lab

We are actively recruiting students and collaborators who want to tackle water and soil contamination with rigorous, practical science.

The EC² Lab is designed to be collaborative, inclusive, and curiosity-driven. We value careful experiments, clear communication, community relevance, and technologies that work outside idealized laboratory conditions.

Open Positions

PhD

Ph.D. Students

Actively recruiting doctoral students starting Fall 2026 in non-thermal plasma systems, PFAS destruction, 3D-printed adsorbents, agricultural water reuse, and circular regeneration.

Full funding may be available for qualified applicants through research assistantships and project funding.
MS

M.S. Students

Master's students can pursue thesis or project-based research in PFAS remediation, water quality analytics, adsorbent characterization, and reactor design.

Research assistantships may be available depending on project fit and funding.
UG

Undergraduate Researchers

K-State undergraduates are welcome for independent study credit, paid research opportunities when available, or volunteer research experience.

Students from engineering, agriculture, chemistry, environmental science, and related fields are encouraged.

What We Look For

  • Curiosity and persistence with difficult environmental problems.
  • Interest in water treatment, soil remediation, materials, plasma, or analytical chemistry.
  • Commitment to inclusive, collaborative research.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.
  • Willingness to engage with agricultural and community stakeholders.

What We Offer

  • Hands-on training in advanced environmental treatment technologies.
  • Interdisciplinary collaborations across K-State and partner institutions.
  • Mentorship shaped by empathy, rigor, and professional development.
  • Opportunities to present, publish, and connect research to real communities.
  • A new lab culture that students will help build from the beginning.

How to Apply

Prospective students and collaborators are encouraged to reach out before submitting a formal application. Email Dr. Choudhary with the subject line Prospective [PhD/MS/UG] Student - [Your Name] and include:

  1. A brief statement of your research interests and how they align with EC² Lab.
  2. Your CV or resume.
  3. Unofficial transcripts, if applying as a student.
  4. Contact information for 2-3 references, if available.
Email Dr. Choudhary

For formal graduate applications, visit the K-State Biological and Agricultural Engineering graduate program.

```
